# Topic 1 — Moran's I {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Are similar values neighbours?

::: {.eq}
I = ( n / Σ w~ij~ ) × Σ~i~Σ~j~ w~ij~ (x~i~ − x̄)(x~j~ − x̄) / Σ~i~ (x~i~ − x̄)²
:::

::: {.incremental}
- Multiply each area's deviation from the mean by its **neighbours'** average deviation (the **lag**), then scale by the variance
- High areas with high neighbours, low with low → products positive → **I > 0**
- Expectation with no pattern: **E[I] = −1/(n−1)**, about 0
:::

| I | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ≈ 0 | no spatial pattern |
| clearly > 0 | **clustering**: similar values are neighbours |
| clearly < 0 | dispersion: neighbours differ (a checkerboard; rare) |

## Four areas by hand

```{r}
v <- c(1, 2, 9, 10)
nb4 <- list(2L, c(1L, 3L), c(2L, 4L), 3L); class(nb4) <- "nb"; attr(nb4, "region.id") <- as.character(1:4)
lw4 <- nb2listw(nb4, style = "W"); z <- v - mean(v)
c(by_hand = (4 / sum(unlist(lw4$weights))) * sum(z * lag.listw(lw4, z)) / sum(z^2), moran_test = unname(moran.test(v, lw4)$estimate[1]))
```

The two large values sit next to each other, so I is strongly positive. The function and the formula agree.

## On the district

```{r}
mi <- moran.test(blocks$dengue_per_100k, lw, zero.policy = TRUE)
mi
```

::: {.key}
Read it from the bottom: **observed I** (about `r round(mi$estimate[1], 2)`), its **expectation** (about 0), and the **z-score and p-value**. Strong positive spatial autocorrelation.
:::

## The permutation (Monte Carlo) test

Shuffle the values over the areas 999 times; how often does a shuffled map beat the real I?

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
set.seed(1)
mc <- moran.mc(blocks$dengue_per_100k, lw, nsim = 999, zero.policy = TRUE)
ggplot(tibble(I = mc$res[-length(mc$res)]), aes(I)) + geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "grey75", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mc$statistic, colour = col_red, linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Moran's I of shuffled maps", title = paste0("Observed I (red) vs 999 shuffles: p = ", mc$p.value))
```

::: {.incremental}
- Assumption-light; usually the better p-value to report
- With 999 shuffles the **smallest p is 0.001**
:::

# Topic 2 — The Moran scatterplot {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Value against the average of its neighbours

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
blocks$z <- as.numeric(scale(blocks$dengue_per_100k)); blocks$lag_z <- lag.listw(lw, blocks$z, zero.policy = TRUE)
ggplot(blocks, aes(z, lag_z)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = high_burden), size = 2.4) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "black") +
  annotate("text", x = c(2.2, -2.2, 2.2, -2.2), y = c(2.2, -2.2, -2.2, 2.2), label = c("High-High", "Low-Low", "High-Low", "Low-High"), colour = "grey40") +
  labs(x = "Rate (standardised)", y = "Neighbours' average (standardised)", colour = NULL)
```

::: {.incremental}
- The **slope of the line is Moran's I** (here `r round(coef(lm(lag_z ~ z, blocks))[["z"]], 2)`)
- **High-High / Low-Low** points make positive autocorrelation
- **High-Low / Low-High** points are **spatial outliers**: LISA (Session 4) finds them
:::

# Topic 3 — Other global tests {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Which global test?

| Test | Question | Variable | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Moran's I** | Are similar values neighbours? | continuous | I > E[I]: clustering |
| **Geary's C** | Are neighbours' *differences* small? | continuous | **C < 1** clustering (opposite of I) |
| **General G** | Do **high** or **low** values cluster? | continuous, positive | G > E[G]: highs cluster |
| **Join counts** | Do same-category areas touch? | binary / categorical | more same-category joins than expected |

## Geary's C, General G, join counts

```{r}
geary.test(blocks$dengue_per_100k, lw, zero.policy = TRUE)$estimate
lw_b <- nb2listw(nb, style = "B", zero.policy = TRUE)
globalG.test(blocks$dengue_per_100k, lw_b, zero.policy = TRUE)$estimate
joincount.test(blocks$high_burden, lw_b, zero.policy = TRUE)[[2]]$estimate
```

::: {.key}
Moran's I is **positive for both hot-spot and cold-spot clustering**. Only **General G** says whether the **high** values are the ones that cluster. Join counts suit a **yes/no** variable.
:::

## Pitfalls

::: {.bad}
- Not saying **which weights**; not saying **which variable** (counts and rates differ)
- **Small areas** give noisy rates, which hides or mimics clustering (smooth with empirical Bayes)
- **Edge effects** and the **modifiable areal unit problem**: a different grouping can change I
- A **trend** (north-south gradient) also gives positive I
- A global test **cannot say where**; a non-significant I can hide a local cluster
:::

## How to report

::: {.good}
*Dengue incidence was strongly clustered across the 79 blocks (global Moran's I = 0.50, queen contiguity, row-standardised weights; permutation p = 0.001, 999 simulations).*
:::

Give the statistic, the weights, the number of simulations and the p-value; then say where, with local methods.

## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s3q1", "Global Moran's I is 0.49 (permutation p = 0.001). What is the best interpretation?",
         c("49% of the variation in the rate is explained by the location",
           "Each area's rate is 0.49 higher than its neighbours' average rate",
           "Neighbouring areas are more alike than expected by chance",
           "About half of all the areas lie in a significant local cluster"), answer = 3,
         explain = "A positive I with a small p-value means similar values are neighbours more often than random. It is not a percentage of variance explained and says nothing about which areas form clusters.")
```

## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s3q2", "What is the expected value of Moran's I when there is no spatial pattern?",
         c("Exactly 1, because every area is its own neighbour",
           "About 0 (exactly −1/(n−1))",
           "Exactly 0.5, halfway between the two extremes",
           "It depends on the data, so there is no expected value"), answer = 2,
         explain = "Under randomness I has expectation −1/(n−1), which is close to 0 for any realistic number of areas.")
```

## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s3q3", "With 999 permutations, what is the smallest possible p-value from moran.mc()?",
         c("0, if the observed I is larger than every one of the shuffled values",
           "0.05, which is the usual cut-off used for a significant result",
           "0.001, as the observed value is one of 1000 arrangements",
           "It varies from one data set to another and has no fixed minimum"), answer = 3,
         explain = "The observed statistic is ranked among the 999 shuffles plus itself, so the best rank gives (0+1)/(999+1) = 0.001.")
```

## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s3q4", "Geary's C is 0.47. How should this be read?",
         c("Neighbours differ strongly, so negative spatial autocorrelation",
           "There is no spatial pattern, because C is not equal to zero",
           "The result is invalid, because C must lie between 0 and 1",
           "Neighbours are similar, so positive spatial autocorrelation"), answer = 4,
         explain = "C is about 1 with no pattern, below 1 with positive autocorrelation and above 1 with negative autocorrelation. It runs in the opposite direction to Moran's I.")
```

## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s3q5", "Moran's I is positive and significant. What does the General G test add?",
         c("Whether high values (hot spots) or low values cluster",
           "The exact location of each separate cluster on the map",
           "A correction of the p-value for the multiple testing",
           "Nothing, because it always gives the same answer as Moran's I"), answer = 1,
         explain = "Both hot-spot and cold-spot clustering give a positive Moran's I. G is above its expectation when high values cluster and below when low values do.")
```
